segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַמּוּרְסָן לְתַרְנְגוֹלִים, אֲבָל חוֹלְטִין. הָאִשָּׁה לֹא תִּשְׁרֶה אֶת הַמּוּרְסָן שֶׁתּוֹלִיךְ בְּיָדָהּ לַמֶּרְחָץ, אֲבָל שָׁפָה הִיא בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יָבֵשׁ. לֹא יִלְעוֹס אָדָם חִיטִּין וְיַנִּיחַ עַל מַכָּתוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מַחְמִיצוֹת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One» may «not soak coarse bran for» feeding «chickens,» lest it be leavened. «However, one» may «pour boiling water» onto the bran before feeding it to the chickens, as it will not become leavened from this brief exposure to water. «A woman» may «not soak coarse bran to bring by hand to the bathhouse» for use as a cleanser; «however, she» may «rub» coarse bran «on her dry skin.» Likewise, the Sages said: «A person» may «not chew wheat and place it on his wound, due to» the fact «that» the wheat «will be leavened» from the saliva and his chewing.

moves.summary: no soaking bran for chickens; scalding allowed
no soaking bran for the bathhouse; rubbing dry allowed
no chewing wheat for a wound, since it leavens

positions.claim: soaking bran or chewing wheat is forbidden on Passover because it leavens; scalding or dry use is permitted
